$$f((x+y)^2)=(x+y)\bigl[f(x)+f(y)\bigr].$$

Let $s=x+y$. The right side depends on $x+y$ only through the prefactor $s$, so $f(x)+f(y)$ must depend only on $x+y$. Setting $y=0$: $f(x)+f(0)=:g(x)$, and the equation $f(x)+f(y)=g(x+y)=f(x+y)+f(0)$ gives
$$f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)+f(0).$$
Define $h(x)=f(x)-f(0)$. Then $h$ is **additive**: $h(x+y)=h(x)+h(y)$, and $f(x)=h(x)+c$ with $c=f(0)$.
